meta.title: Borrow, Learn, Repair: A Library Experiment
meta.source: Original fictional educational passage; not an official IELTS paper
meta.instructions: Questions 1–7: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN. Questions 8–9: choose A, B or C. Questions 10–11: choose a heading i–v for paragraphs C and D. Questions 12–13: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: When Riverton Library launched its Object Lending Corner in 2021, staff expected sewing machines to be popular. Instead, the most frequently borrowed items in the first month were portable projectors. The collection later expanded to include board games, sewing machines and digital thermometers. Each object could be borrowed for seven days with a library card, and no borrowing fee was charged. The project grew from conversations with residents who wanted equipment for occasional tasks but hesitated to buy products they might use only once or twice. The library did not advertise the project as a substitute for local shops.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: At first, librarians worried about objects being damaged or returned late. There were 18 reports of minor damage during the first quarter. Staff then introduced ten-minute demonstrations and illustrated instruction cards, showing borrowers how to operate the most delicate items. In the following quarter, the number of damage reports fell to nine. The library did not claim that the change alone had caused the reduction. Its budget for spare parts remained unchanged, and some larger objects still developed waiting lists because staff needed extra time to inspect them after each return.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: To bring more people into the project, the library began repair workshops on the second Saturday of each month. The sessions were open to residents whether or not they held a library card. Volunteers helped visitors examine small household goods, while reminding them that some problems were unsafe to tackle without a professional. Desk lamps were brought in more often than any other item; broken zips and headphones were also common. The workshops had no minimum age requirement, and staff did not record the ages of visitors. Their main aim was to help people understand why objects stopped working, even if they could not be fixed that day.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Six months into the pilot, the library collected feedback through a questionnaire completed by 120 participants. Of these, 74 said they had bought fewer new household products since joining the scheme. These were self-reported habits, and the team had not measured any change in carbon emissions. Some respondents said it was inconvenient to cross town to return bulky objects. To address this, librarians proposed testing collection lockers near the train station the following year. The proposal was still under review when the report was written, and no lockers had been installed. The library planned a second survey before deciding whether to expand the programme.

questions.prompt: The Object Lending Corner began in 2021.

evidence.quote: launched its Object Lending Corner in 2021

questions.explanation_zh: 原文明确说明该项目于2021年启动，题干与原文一致。

questions.prompt: Borrowers can keep every object for fourteen days.

evidence.quote: Each object could be borrowed for seven days

questions.explanation_zh: 题干是14天，原文是7天，存在明确冲突。

questions.prompt: The library charges a fee each time an object is borrowed.
questions.explanation_zh: 原文明确表示免收借用费，与题干相反。

questions.prompt: Every volunteer at the repair workshops is a qualified electrician.

evidence.quote: Volunteers helped visitors examine small household goods

questions.explanation_zh: 原文只说志愿者协助检查物品，未交代其职业资质；不能推断他们全是电工，也无法证实相反说法。

questions.prompt: The spare-parts budget increased after the library introduced instruction cards.

evidence.quote: Its budget for spare parts remained unchanged

questions.explanation_zh: 原文说明备件预算保持不变，与“increased”直接冲突。

questions.prompt: The library has already installed collection lockers near the train station.
questions.explanation_zh: 原文明确说尚未安装储物柜，题干的already与此相反。

questions.prompt: Most repair-workshop visitors were older than forty.

evidence.quote: staff did not record the ages of visitors

questions.explanation_zh: 原文没有收集访客年龄数据，因此无法判断是否大多数人超过40岁。

questions.prompt: Which item was borrowed most often during the first month?

evidence.quote: the most frequently borrowed items in the first month were portable projectors

questions.explanation_zh: 原文的the most frequently borrowed与题干most often形成同义对应，答案是portable projectors。

questions.prompt: What change happened before the number of minor damage reports fell?

evidence.quote: Staff then introduced ten-minute demonstrations and illustrated instruction cards

questions.explanation_zh: 工作人员先提供简短演示和图示说明卡，之后损坏报告减少。原文仅说明先后关系，没有单独证明因果。

options.A: An increase in the spare-parts budget

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for paragraph C.

evidence.quote: Their main aim was to help people understand why objects stopped working

questions.explanation_zh: C段核心是社区维修活动及其教学目的，因此选择“通过社区维修学习”。

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for paragraph D.

evidence.quote: The proposal was still under review when the report was written

questions.explanation_zh: D段先谈参与者反馈，再谈仍在审核中的取还方案，因此选择“反馈与待评估方案”。

questions.prompt: Which objects were brought to the repair workshops most often?

evidence.quote: Desk lamps were brought in more often than any other item

questions.explanation_zh: most often对应more often than any other item，直接抄写desk lamps，满足不超过两词。

questions.prompt: How many participants completed the questionnaire?
questions.explanation_zh: 题干问完成问卷的人数，直接定位completed by 120 participants。
